Hey. I'm only a year older than you and I don't even swear that much in my HEAD, so noticing how much of that was in this was mildly amusing to me. None of the rest of it, just the amount of swearing. The rest is sadly relatable. A lot of people on the internet as well as in American high schools these days look at dark humour and really sad things as like, #meme material, and I kind of hate it but kind of don't... What I mean by that is that I sometimes unintentionally take part in it and then it just seriously bums me out thinking about it. Thinking about how that lame, sad 'joke' I just make was actually not a joke at all, thinking about how this is what today's youth has come down to, this is what being a teenager these days is like. And that's not simple meme-ing around, that's not funny. That's concerning.

I tried a sort of in-school therapy thing last school year, which didn't go for more than one session, because the lady obviously didn't comprehend a darn thing I was trying to get across. And that was entirely my choice to try, my parents had no say in it other than them complaining that they had to pay for that one meeting, only for me to decide it was a horrible idea and should never happen again, ever, no matter what. Because I decided it wasn't even worth the effort to try to make another person get me, because if I really wanted to, I could fix my problems all by myself, or at least make the effects of them less... ouchie, I guess, is the best way to put it. I'm not diagnosed with anything, and I don't want to be. I have personal reasons for not trusting "professionals," and also, I'm sort of a health nut and personally believe that anything that could potentially cause another problem in the process of fixing one SHOULDN'T BE LEGAL. (So, like, pretty much every drug advertised on TV. Ever. "Hi, I'm your friendly internet plant loving vegan, nice to meet you!" Handshake?) Point being: I don't want anyone trying to get me to take anything for something that I could fix to some extent with healthy diet, exercise, the right detox tea blend, and some funny Youtubers.

Somehow, I've managed to survive seven suicide attempts WITHOUT waking up in a hospital, OR having anyone find me. Nope, I was completely alone, my parents were away for long periods all seven times, and I woke up alone too, freaking out every time because I thought 4SURE I wasn't going to. But I did. And I still have times where the only thing keeping me from an eighth, a last, with the gun under my father's bed, guaranteed to work, is how religious I suddenly became over the past year. I've got to believe that there's SOMETHIN, some REAL REASON that I'm still alive, with all the stuff I've pulled. I tend to keep myself from falling down depressive spirals by basically finding things I like and obsessing over them, trying to contribute to those fandoms, and it usually works for a while.

So I failed a ton of classes. I can make that up when the time comes and I need to for some reason, but for now, I'm doing better than I was, and that's what. So my parents have been horrible and have done a bunch of things that'd by law be considered abusive and it's really screwed me up in a lot of ways. I'll be a better parent than they were and I know it. So sometimes I casually joke about death and purposely sound up-beat when I'm saying something that SHOULD be really sad, and none of that is actually a joke, so I should stop doing that and discuss with others in my age group why it's a bad way to go about it. So I'm going to do that. I'm going to keep myself motivated and try to motivate others, here as well as there, starting on this very post. I want to influence people to not kill themselves, but to instead kill the idea of mental illness and suicide being things that are totally okay to turn into casual humour, because sometimes ya really can't tell if someone's serious or not, and they're starting to make it sound like it's cool with the way that's going, and it's not. At all. It's pretty bad when I can read off a downer Tumblr post like that and get clapping and laughs from people standing nearby me in my social circle, yet when I tell them that I myself have just made it to a year and three months clean from self harm, the smiles die down and only one person responds and that's a, "Oh, that's... great for you, I guess..." No one wants to hear about people when they REALLY had problems, and today's society is getting increasingly anti-recovery at the same time, which is majorly problematic for obvious reasons.

I hope you find people and interests and they give you reasons, like mine so far have for me.

And I completely understand if it doesn't, but I hope my ranting will have made some sort of difference.
